key_insight: A rule-based computable phenotype that combines structured EHR data with clinical notes can improve MASLD identification in patients with type 2 diabetes.
clinical_relevance: Better phenotyping could help researchers and health systems more reliably find MASLD cases in T2D populations for screening, cohort building, and outcomes studies.
method: Built five complementary phenotype algorithms using fibrosis indices and liver injury biomarkers.
Added lightweight NLP to detect MASLD mentions in clinical notes with keyword matching, context filtering, and negation detection.
Evaluated performance across multiple thresholds and validated findings with age/sex-stratified analyses and manual chart review.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic evaluation across threshold settings plus manual chart review and stratified analyses, supporting real-world feasibility and accuracy.
watch_item: Performance may depend on note quality, site-specific documentation patterns, and the portability of rule-based thresholds across health systems.
paper_title: Improving MASLD Identification in Patients with T2D: A Computable Phenotype Framework Integrating Structured Data and Clinical Notes
